literal_meaning: ঘরে লক্ষ্মীকে আনা (bringing the goddess Lakshmi into the house)
figurative_meaning_en: To bring a daughter-in-law into the family
similar_in_english: No direct equivalent; akin to 'marrying off one's son' or 'welcoming a bride home'
example_sentences_in_bangla: বিয়ের পর ঘরে লক্ষ্মী এলে সংসার সুখী হয়।
example_sentences_in_english: They will soon bring Lakshmi home.
The family becomes prosperous after bringing Lakshmi into the home through marriage.
history: The idiom references the Hindu goddess Lakshmi, symbolizing wealth and good fortune. In Bengali culture, a daughter-in-law is metaphorically seen as Lakshmi entering the household to bring prosperity and happiness.
note: This expression reflects traditional views on arranged marriages and the auspicious role of women in the family.
